Palaeomagnetism of Precambrian rocks from Gabon, Congo craton, Africa 
MANOEL SOUZA D’AGRELLA-FILHO’, JEAN-LOUIS FEYBESSEZ, JEAN-PIERRE l’RIAN2, DIDIER DUPUISz

Abstract - Palaeomagnetlc results for 75 orientated hand samples (25 sampling sites) from the Ggooue series 
amphibolites (Z’), Archean basement amphibolites and gramdites (14) and Precambrian dolerite dykes (34) are 
presented. Magnelization of many amphibolites showed unstable directions during alternating field (AF) and 
thermal demagnetization experimenk and no directions of magnetization could be isolated. However, a character- 
istic direction could be isolated in a few amphibolite sites and for the granulites studied. The best group of site 
mean directions Cm=EiQ”, Im=69” (x=27, ass=W, N=4) yielded a palaeomagnetic pole located at 44O E, 19” N 
(K=lO, A%=300). This pole is close to a palaeomagnetic pole obtained for granulites from the Jequie complex (So 
Francisco craton) dated by the %r/sAr method as 2.0 Ga, suggesting that both areas belonged to the same tec- 
tonic unit at that time. ‘Ihe unmetamorphosed dolerite dykes (5) displayed multi-component behavior, but a com- 
mon characteristic direction could be isolated for four dykes,, Dm=262O, Im=49“ (x=13, aw=27“, N=4), which 
yielded a palaeomagnetic pole located at 72” E, B” N (K=9; Ass=33O). However, this pole is different from those ob- 
tained for dyke swarms in Brazil, which are supposedly of comparable age.

INTRODUCTION 
The present Palaeoproterozoic palaeomagnetic data 
from the Kalahari Craton (southern Africa) enabled the 
definition of a fairly well-established apparent polar 
wander (APW) path during the time interval between 
2.05 Ga and 1.85 Ga for this cratonic unit (Morgan, 
1985; Hatting, 1989). 
Several well dated palaeomagnetic poles from the 
Amazonian and West African cratons in the 2.05-1.8 
Ga time interval led Onstott and Dorbor (1987) and 
Renne et al. (1988) to suggest that these cratonic units 
were separated from the Kalahari craton at that time. 
However, only a few palaeomagnetic poles of Pa- 
laeoproterozoic age are presently available for the 
intervening !%o Francisco/Congo cratonic area. 
Unmetamorphosed dykes of Meso- to Neopro- 
terozoic age from the eastern S&o Francisco craton 
(Salvador and Ilheus-Olivenca dykes), yielded com- 
patible geochemical, geochronological(4oAr/39Ar) and 
palaeomagnetic results defining an APW path for the 
so Francisco craton during the interval 1.08-1.01 Ga 
(d’Agrella-Filho et al., 1989,199O). 
Mafic dykes outcropping in Gabon (Africa) have 
been correlated with the Salvador and Ilh&.rs- 
Olivenca dyke swarms, on a pm-drift configuration, 
based on geological and geochronological evidence 
(Renne et al., 1990). According to these authors, the 
Mayumbian basin of the Congo craton, where a 4-5 
km thick sequence of basalts and rhyolites has been 
deposited, could be the magma feeder source for the 
Brazilian dykes and also the mafic dykes of similar

age (1.0 Ga) cutting the Francevillean Group in Ga- 
bon. This magma source would geographically agree 
with the northern north-south striking swarm at Sal- 
vador, the western east-west striking swarm at Il- 
heus-Olivenca and the northeastern east-northeast 
striking swarm at Gabon. Also, recent geochemical 
analysis of the Gabon dykes shows that they are 
similar to the Brazilian dykes (Enzo Piccirillo, pers. 
comm., 1994). 
The main objective of this study was to obtain pa- 
laeomagnetic results from selected rock formations 
on the Congo craton and compare them with those 
for rocks of similar age from the S&o Francisco craton. 
These results can then be used for paleogeographic 
reconstructions of these cratonic areas and may help 
to elucidate the evolution of the Palaeoproterozoic 
Gabon mobile belt, previously interpreted as a suture 
zone (Ledru et al., 1989). For this purpose, it is impor- 
tant to compare palaeomagnetic results from the 
cratonic areas from both sides of the mobile belt, be- 
fore, during and after its evolution. 
GEOLOGICAL SETTING AND SAMPLING 
The Precambrian of Gabon is divided into three 
units; the Archean basement, the Palaeoproterozoic 
and the Neoproterozoic (Fig. 1). 
The Archean shield area consists mainly of 
polyphase medium- to high-grade banded gneisses 
and greenstone belts with Fe bearing formations, 
metamorphosed at 3.15 Ga and intruded by grani- 
toids at around 3.0-2.6 Ga.

Figure 2 (a) Wulff stereographic projection [open (full) symbols represent upward (downward) 
inclinations] and (b) Ziljerveld diagram [open (full) circles represent vertical (horizontal) plane 
projections] of magnetization directions during treatment for sample OG4A1, site !33. 8 and 6B 
represent the present geomagnetic field and the present dipolar field, respectively. 
The Palaeoproterozoic is represented by the 
Francevillian sedimentary rocks (2.3-2.0 Ga) and the 
Ogooue fold and thrust belt. Resting unconformably 
over the Archean basement, the Francevillian is a 
dominantly elastic series of uraniferous conglomer- 
ates and sandstones, arkosic sandstones with layer 
intervals of cherts and manganese oxides and, locally, 
volcanic deposits. 
The Ogooue erogenic belt consists mainly of meta- 
sediments and volcanic rocks considered to be Palae- 
oproterozoic in age. Locally, slices of reworked Ar- 
chean rocks have been tectonically incorporated. The 
metamorphic and structural features are consistent 
with the collision tectonics of the Ebumean cycle (2.2- 
1.9 Ga). 
The Upper Proterozoic consists mainly of the 
Nyanga and Mayombe sediments. To the west, the 
Mayombe Pan-African belt is composed of Neopro- 
terozoic sediments and reworked Archean and Pa- 
laeoproterozoic basement rocks that overthrust the 
Nyanga Series. 
Several dolerite dykes intrude the Lower Proterozoic

and Archean terrains. A dolerite dyke from Mikou-

Three concordant results, one on whole rock and two 
on fekispathic fractions, yielded ages between 995f15 
Ma and 977S4 Ma (reference in Cahen et al., 1984). 
Field work was carried out in Gabon in August, 
1990. Seventy five orientated hand samples from 25 
sites were collected for palaeomagnetic analysis (Fig. 
1). Twenty seven samples (9 sites) are from amphibo- 
lites from the Ogooue Series. Nine amphibolite sam- 
ples (4 sites) and 5 granulite samples (two sites) are 
from the Archean basement Thirty four samples (ten 
sites) are from metamorphosed and unmetamorphosed 
dykes. Whenever possible, both solar and magnetic 
compasses were used for orientating the samples. 
PROCEDURE 
Samples were treated using standard palaeomag- 
netic procedures. Three to four cylindrical specimens 
with diameter and height equal to 2.5 cm were cut 
from cores drilled from every hand sample. Altemat- 
ing field (AF) and thermal demagnetization experi- 
ments were applied to isolate magnetization compo- 
nents and to test the stability of remnance. 
Generally, steps of 2.5, 5 or 10 mT up to 100 mT

(a) 
Figure 5. zijderveld diagrams and w&f stereographic projection for samples (a, b) OG-75- 
Dl, site S2 and (c, d) OG-B-Al, site Sl (Anzhean granulites). Same conventi~ as for Fig. 2. 
were used for AF treatment and steps of 50°C up to 
500°C followed by the sequence 530°C, 55OT, 57O”C, 
6OOT, 63OT, 650°C and 670°C (or 680°C) were used 
for thermal treatment. This procedure was inter- 
rupted whenever the sample remnant magnetization 
behaved unstably. Sometimes a combination of AF 
followed by thermal demagnetization was applied 
(Roy and Lapointe, 1978). 
A spinner magnetometer (Molspin) and a suscep- 
tibility meter (Sapphire instruments) were used for 
measurements of the remnant magnetization and 
magnetic susceptibility. Thermomagnetic curves were 
obtained for several samples using a horizontal mag- 
netic balance. 
Stereographic (Wulff) and orthogonal (Zijderveld, 
1967) projections were used to separate magnetiza- 
tions present in rocks and the principal component 
analysis was used to determine directions (Kirshvink, 
2980). Only directions defined by at least 4 points and 
with MAD smaller than 10’ were considered. Fisher 
(1953) statistics was used to determine mean direc- 
tions and palaeomagnetic poles.

PALAEOMAGNETIC RESULTS 
Ogoou6 Series 
The 27 amphibohs from the Ogoou6 Series 
yielded natural remnant magnetization (NRM) in- 
tensities ranging from lo-4 A m-l to values as high as 
20 A m-l and volumetric susceptibiIities in the range 
6xlW13 (SI units). The magnetization of most sam- 
ples behaved unstably during AF and thermaI treat- 
ment (Fig. 2) and it was not possible to resolve their 
magnetization components. This was the case for sites 
S7 (OG-1 to 3), S8 (OG-4 to 6), SlO (OG-10 to 12), S12 
(OG-16 to 18), S13 (OG-50 to 52) and S14 (OG-99 to 
101) (Table 1). Magnetic vector components were ob- 
tained from three sites of the Ogoouk Series (sites S9, 
Sll and 515). Specimens from site 99 (OG-7 and OG-9) 
yielded a southeastern direction with steep upward 
in&nation after AF treatment (OG-9-Bl; Fig. 3a, d). 
SeveraI specimens of samples from sites Sll (Fig. 
3b, d; OGWBl) and S15 (Fig. 3c, d; OG-103-Cl) 
yieIded a northeastem direction with steep downward 
in&nation after AF and thermaI titments. Specimens 
from sampIes OG-15 and OG-102 behaved unstabIy 
and only for specimen OG15-Cl was it possibIe to 
isoIate the nor&as&m direclion mentioned above.

The nine Archean amphibohs yielded NRM

Basement granulites 
The five basement granulites sampled from two 
sites (Sl and S2) yielded NRM intensities ranging from 
1 to 10 A m-1 and susceptibilities in the range 6.3xlW 
0.12 (SI units). A stable east-northeast direction with 
steep downward inclination could be isolated for all 
samples after AF and thermal treatment (Fig. 5). 
Dolerite dykes 
The dolerite dykes were analysed palaeomagneti- 
tally and geochemically at the University of Trieste 
by Enzo Piccirillo. Thin sections of the dykes showed 
that only five of them were unmetamorphosed, the re 
mainder are metamorphosed to amphibolite facies. The 
&metamorphosed dykes are geochemically similar to 
those from Salvador and Ilheus-Olivenqa in Brazil. These 
dykes correspond to lati-basalt, andesi-basalt and tholei- 
ite rocks (E. Piccirillo, F. wmm., 1994). 
Metamorphosed dykes 
The metamorphic dykes show NRM intensities 
ranging from lo” to 10-* A m-1 and susceptibilities in 
the range 4x10-5-lo-4 (CGS units). Several samples be- 
haved unstably during AF and thermal treatments. 
This was the case for samples from sites S17 and S19. 
Relatively stable directions could be isolated for 
samples from sites S16, S18 and S20, although no 
consistency between site mean directions was ob 
tained. Figures 6 and 7 show examples of the mag- 
netic behavior yielded for each of these sites, Direc- 
tions with approximately opposite polarities were 
isolated for two samples from the same dyke (Fig. 7). 
Unmetamorphosed dykes 
The unmetamorphosed dykes have NRM intensi- 
ties ranging from 1 to 30 A m-1 and susceptibilities in 
the range 1.9x10-24.7x10-* (SI units). The AF treat- 
ment provided better results than the thermal treat- 
ment and the majority of the samples showed multi- 
component behavior. Thermomagnetic plots are 
typical of rocks with poor-Ti titanomagnetites (Fig. 8) 
with Curie temperatures between 544°C and 582°C. 
Four dykes yielded either a western direction with 
moderate to high upward inclination or an eastern 
direction with moderate to high downward inclina- 
tion (Figs 9 and 10). Although other directions with 
higher coercivities were also present, they have not 
yielded consistent within-site results. Samples from 
the 5” unmetamorphosed dykes (site S24) yielded 
multicomponent behavior after AF treatment (Fig. 
11). However, none of these directions were found in 
samples from other sites. 
DISCUSSION 
The palaeomagnetic results obtained in this study 
are summam& in Table 1. Amphibolites from the 
Ogooue Series were metamorphosed during the devel- 
opment of the Ogooue mobile belt (Ledru et al., 1989) 
during the Ebumean cycle and are Palaeoproterozoic 
in age. A Rb/Sr regression line based on five musco- 
vites from pegmatites cutting the Ogooue system in an 
area defined by 11”24’-ll%YE and 0’45’-1Y2’S yielded 
an age of ca 1990 Ma (I.R. of 0.700), which post-dates 
the metamorphism of the series (Vachette, 1964). The 
Archean amphibolites and granulites are geographi- 
cally situated inside or at the boundary of the craton 
next to the Ogooue belt and were probably affected by 
the Eburnean cycle. At this cratonic margin, the 
Francevillian sediments (Booue basin) have undergone 
a deformation phase accompanied by low-grade 
metamorphism (Ledru et al., 1989). 
Petrographical analyses of the dolerite dykes 
showed that half of the dykes were metamorphosed 
to amphibolite facies. The geographical proximity of 
both metamorphosed and unmetamorphosed dykes 
(Fig. 1) suggests different origins for them and, con- 
sequently, different ages for these two groups of 
dykes, The metamorphic dykes are older than the 
unmetamorphosed dykes and a possible age for the 
metamorphism of these dykes would be the Palaeo- 
proterozoic Ebumean cycle. 
Most of the amphibolites showed unstable behav- 
ior during AF and thermal treatments. However, it 
was possible to isolate stable directions for amphi- 
bolites from three sites of the Ogooue Series. Also, 
some amphibolites from the Archean basement (two 
sites) and some amphibolite dykes (3 sites) yielded

stable directions (Table 11). As described earlier, the

these amphibolites and granulites are shown in Fig. 
12a. Virtual geomagnetic poles (VGPs) were calcu-

of site mean directions is obtained with sites Sl, S2, 
Sll and S15 (Fig. 12a) where two sites (Sll and S15) 
correspond to amphibolites from the Ogooue Series 
(Palaeoproterozoic) and. two sites (Sl and S2) are 
basement gram&es. ,lllthough these directions 
were isolated for rocks of different lithologies and 
no radiometric ages are presently available for 
them, the results are very similar to those obtained 
for granulites from the Archean Jequie granulitic 
complex (Brazil), which was affected by the 
Transamazonian cycle (equivalent to the Ebumean 
cycle). The calculated mean direction obtained for 
these four sites of gram&es and amphibolites from 
Gabon, Dm-54.0”; Im=68.6” (~=27.5; a95 =17.8”), 
yielded a palaeomagnetic pole located at 44.3” E; 
19.0” N (K=10.5; A95=29.8”; pole !SOG in Fig. 13). 
This pole, in a pre-drift diagram, is very close to a 
preliminary pole calculated for granulites from the 
Jequie complex (JC, Fig. 13), which was dated by 
the mAr/s9Ar method yielding concordant ages of 
1994*16 Ma (biotite) and 201%25 Ma (hornblende) 
for two sites (Sletten, 1989). 
The S9 VGP (Fig. 13) from another amphibolite 
site from the Ogooue Series is closer to the pole ob- 
tained for Lower Proterozoic dykes situated next to 
the town of Uaud in Bahia State, S&o Francisco

Three possible explanations for this inconsistency CONCLUSIONS 
are: 
i) this component of magnetization is of secondary 
origin - this explanation is coherent with the fact that 
other directions, although inconsistent, are identified 
in many samples of these dykes; 
ii) these dykes did not correspond to those from 
Salvador and Ih#us-Olivenca, having different ages; 
iii) The difference between the poles corresponds 
to relative movements between the two areas. 
Lower Proterozoic amphibolites from the Ogooue 
Series, amphibolites and gram&es from the Archean 
basement and dolerite dykes from Gabon (Congo cra- 
ton) were analysed palaeomagnetically. Although a 
complicated response to AF and thermal treatments 
was obtained for these rocks, with many samples 
showing unstable behavior, it was possible to draw 
some conchrsions about these results.

### page_14
M. S. D’AGRELLA-FILHO et al. 
(a) 
Figure 12 Site mean directions. (a) amphibolites from the Ogooue Series 
(squares); Archean amphibolites (diamonds); basement granulites 
(triangles); metamorphic dykes (circles). @) unmetamorphosed dolerite 
dykes. Wulff stereographic projection. Same conventions as for Fig. 2. 
The analysis showed that granulites present better 
response to AF and thermal treatments than amphi- 
bolites. The same conclusion was obtained analysing 
amphibolites and gram&es from the !%o Francisco 
craton. 
Characteristic directions were isolated for some of 
the amphibolite sites and for the two basement 
granulites sites. Although some (or all) of these di- 
rections could represent later overprints, a palaeo- 
magnetic pole (!SOG in Fig. 13) determined for the 
best group of mean site directions (two sites of am- 
phibolites from the Ogooue Series and two sites of 
granulites) is located very close to the pole obtained 
for gram&es from the Jequie complex (So Francisco 
craton), probably of 2.0 Ga (pole JC in Fig. 13), sug- 
gesting that these areas could belong to the same unit 
at this time. 
The unmetamorphosed Neoproterozoic dolerite 
dykes yielded a common characteristic direction for 
four of these dykes. The palaeomagnetic pole (with a 
high value of 1~95) calculated for these characteristic 
directions is very different from those determined for 
the dyke swarms from Salvador and Ilht%rs-Olivenca 
in Brazil (Fig. 14).
